title: Saying It Another Way
text:
Writers often restate an idea in different words to make it clearer. This technique, known as paraphrasing, allows a reader to understand a complex point without repeating the original sentence. A good paraphrase keeps the same meaning while changing the structure and vocabulary.

However, not every restatement is equivalent to the original. A careless paraphrase can alter the meaning or make an ambiguous claim sound certain. For this reason, editors check whether a restated sentence truly clarifies the author's intention.

questions.text: What does a good paraphrase keep the same?
According to the second paragraph, what can a careless paraphrase do?
options: Alter the meaning of the original

questions.text: Why do editors check restated sentences?
options: To make sure they really clarify what the author meant
To count the number of words

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's view of paraphrasing?
options: It is useful but must be done carefully
It is only useful for poets

vocabulary.definition: expressing the meaning of a text in different words
having the same value or meaning
having more than one possible meaning

paragraph_translations: Os escritores costumam reformular uma ideia com palavras diferentes para torná-la mais clara. Essa técnica, conhecida como parafraseamento, permite que o leitor compreenda um ponto complexo sem repetir a frase original. Uma boa paráfrase mantém o mesmo significado, mas muda a estrutura e o vocabulário.

No entanto, nem toda reformulação é equivalente ao original. Uma paráfrase descuidada pode alterar o significado ou fazer uma afirmação ambígua soar como certa. Por isso, os editores verificam se a frase reformulada realmente esclarece a intenção do autor.
